SEBoK Modeling and Simulation, Distilled

Third-batch distillation, batch 1 doc 4. The SEBoK carries modeling-and-simulation content distributed across multiple knowledge areas; the dedicated Modeling and Simulation page returned 404 at retrieval, and the content is reconstructed from the apparatus (especially SE-080 Principle 5 "the real system is the perfect representation of the system"). Modeling and simulation is structurally a Cluster H (hypostatic boundary) discipline at engagement scope: every model is a representation, never the modeled. M&S is also Cluster G (specialty engineering) when read as the engineering specialty whose practice is the construction and use of representations. The modeling-vs-simulation distinction (static structure vs. dynamic behavior) is a universal-sibling pair (Cluster A) at the representation rung. Editorial note: page-not-found state is recorded; structural reading uses adjacent material. Three corpus forms compose; the article is editorially thin but structurally important as the canonical Cluster H worked example.

II. Source Read

Editorial note. The dedicated SEBoK Modeling and Simulation page is not directly retrievable at the canonical URL or at structurally adjacent variants (Modeling and Simulation in Systems Engineering, Modeling) as of the 2026-04-30 retrieval. The SEBoK distributes modeling-and-simulation content across multiple knowledge areas in Part 2 (Foundations) and Part 3 (SE and Management); the SE-080 SEPAT-principles distillation captured Principle 5 ("the real system is the perfect representation of the system") as the SEBoK's own community-native articulation of the modeling-and-simulation discipline. The structural reading below proceeds from that articulation plus general SE-community knowledge that modeling-and-simulation comprises (a) static structural models, (b) dynamic behavioral simulations, (c) physics-based simulations, (d) discrete-event simulations, and (e) agent-based simulations, with purposes spanning analysis, design, verification, validation, training, and operations.

III. Structural Read

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372). Modeling-and-simulation is the canonical Cluster H worked example. Every model is rung-2 representation of a rung-1 substrate; the model is never the thing. SE-080 Principle 5 supplies the SEBoK's own community-native articulation: "the real system is the perfect representation of the system" — meaning no model can substitute for the modeled. The discipline of modeling-and-simulation is the disciplined production of representations whose limits are explicitly tracked. Doc 372's apparatus is not external to M&S; it tracks discipline the M&S community already practices.

Cluster G (SIPE / specialty engineering, SE-065). Modeling-and-simulation is itself a specialty engineering discipline at the representation rung. M&S engineers compose with reliability engineers, safety engineers, security engineers, and others under the umbrella of specialty engineering (SE-065 enumeration). M&S supplies the representational substrate against which other specialties evaluate the system. Cluster G densifies; this batch is targeted at G, and M&S is one of its members.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D). The modeling-vs-simulation distinction (static structural representation vs. dynamic behavioral representation) is a two-member universal-sibling pair at the representation rung. Each member binds every M&S engagement as one aspect-of-representation. Sub-axes (physics-based, discrete-event, agent-based) extend the lattice. Cluster A admits the M&S case as a small-cardinality instance.

Cluster D (co-production at sub-rungs, Doc 573). A model is co-produced between the modeled-system substrate (rung-1) and the modeler's purpose (rung-2 affordance: what is being analyzed). Neither alone produces the model.
